# From OECD extract to analysis-ready data

We downloaded 1,359 records from the OECD **Research and Innovation Careers Observatory (ReICO)**, covering 36 countries. The data describe six aspects of work and well-being across different education levels and age groups.

## Where the data come from

ReICO does not rely on a single survey sent directly to Master's and doctorate holders. National contact points compile aggregated statistics from official sources, including labour-force and graduate surveys, population censuses, and administrative records on education, employment and taxation. The OECD processes these submissions and cross-checks them against international data sources where possible.

The target population comprises residents aged 25–64. Results are reported for Master's and doctorate holders, with further breakdowns by age group.

## How we prepared the data

The downloaded indicator codes contained information about three variables:

- **Education level:** total population, Master's degree or doctorate
- **Age group:** total population aged 25–64, or the groups 25–34, 35–44, 45–54 and 55–64
- **Measure:** gross annual earnings, annual hours worked, permanent contracts, happiness, financial satisfaction or satisfaction with leisure time

To prepare the data for analysis, we decoded the OECD indicator labels, standardised country names and used the OECD observation-status metadata to resolve repeated records. We then reorganised the data so that each row represents one country, education level and age group.

The final dataset contains 375 such combinations, with the six measures arranged in separate columns.

[Read the OECD ReICO methodology](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/about/programmes/oecd-data-collection-programme/science-technology-and-innovation/reico/oecd-reico-guidelines.pdf){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

[Visit the OECD ReICO database](https://data-explorer.oecd.org/vis?df%5Bag%5D=OECD.STI.STP&df%5Bds%5D=DisseminateFinalDMZ&df%5Bid%5D=DSD_REICO_FULL%40DF_RDL&lc=en){.btn .btn-outline-primary}


::: {.callout-important}
## A note on interpretation

All data refer to 2022. Income values are not always reported in a standardised currency, so direct comparisons between countries should be interpreted with caution.
:::
